clue.text: Artist acquires constituency

parts.note: to acquire is to gain, so acquires gives gains
a borough is a town that once sent its own member to Parliament, an electoral constituency

explanation.surface: A painter wins a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough was the eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was a celebrated English painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Kings of Victorian literature

parts.note: British kings have often borne one first name, and several Victorian novelists (Eliot, Meredith, Gissing, MacDonald) bore it too

explanation.surface: Who ruled the roost among nineteenth-century writers?
explanation.walkthrough: Four Hanoverian kings shared the name; so did George Eliot, George Meredith and George Gissing, which makes them the 'kings' of Victorian letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural first name covers several British monarchs and several Victorian novelists, notably George Eliot and George Meredith.

clue.text: Not what the Impressionists did, surely?

definitions.text: Not what the Impressionists did, surely?

parts.words: Not what the Impressionists did, surely?
parts.note: an impressionist mimics people, but the Impressionist painters broke with copying nature faithfully

explanation.surface: Monet and his circle surely did not merely copy what they saw.
explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic turn is on 'impressionist': a stage impressionist copies voices, while the painters set out to record an impression rather than a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy or mimic is what a stage impressionist does, the opposite of what the painters claimed.

clue.text: Combination of ideas in dissertation on Thorndyke's smuggling vicar?

indicators.note: on joins the two pieces, the dissertation put next to the vicar's name

parts.note: Dr Syn, the smuggling vicar of Dymchurch, is the hero of Russell Thorndike's novels
a dissertation is a thesis

explanation.surface: A scholarly paper about a fictional clergyman who runs contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Syn is the vicar-smuggler of Russell Thorndike's novels (the clue spells the author Thorndyke), set on Romney Marsh in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy a synthesis is a fusion of thesis and antithesis, a merging of separate notions into one whole.

clue.text: Mary McCarthy's refreshment centre on the sands?

definitions.text: Mary McCarthy's refreshment centre on the sands?

parts.words: Mary McCarthy's refreshment centre on the sands?
parts.note: Mary McCarthy wrote a 1949 satirical novella about a utopian colony, titled after a fertile spot in a desert

explanation.surface: Where would the American novelist stop for a drink at the beach?
explanation.walkthrough: Mary McCarthy's novella 'The Oasis' (1949) satirises a utopian community; a desert watering hole is the 'refreshment centre on the sands'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spring in a desert gives travellers water and rest, and it is also the title of McCarthy's novella.

clue.text: By the help of canvas wings … proposes to fly — - -from Dover to Calais " (The Fool of Quality, Henry Brooke)

definitions.text: By the help of canvas wings … proposes to fly — - -from Dover to Calais " (The Fool of Quality, Henry Brooke)

parts.words: By the help of canvas wings … proposes to fly — - -from Dover to Calais " (The Fool of Quality, Henry Brooke)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Henry Brooke's novel: the missing hyphenated word means across the water, as a flight from Dover to Calais crosses the Channel

explanation.surface: A line from an eighteenth-century novel about flying across the Channel on sails.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Brooke's sentence: a flight from Dover to Calais goes across the English Channel, so the word needed means across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means beyond or across the water, as a crossing from Dover to Calais is.

clue.text: Puppet embodying the spirit of 20, may be grand in melodrama

definitions.meaning: a Lyon puppet character of anarchic mischief, the spirit of disorder of 20 down
the Grand ... was a Paris theatre of gory melodrama

explanation.surface: A marionette full of mayhem who could star in a lurid stage thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Guignol is the French puppet of Lyon, a Punch-like rebel; the Paris Théâtre du Grand Guignol gave its name to blood-soaked melodrama.
explanation.definitionFit: The French puppet of Lyon is a rowdy rebel, and with 'Grand' before it names horror melodrama on stage.

clue.text: Permit trivia, perhaps, in Rousseau's work

indicators.note: perhaps marks the words before it as one possible arrangement of letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Allowing trifles into the writings of the philosopher of Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rousseau' suggests Jean-Jacques the philosopher, but this is Henri Rousseau, the self-taught naive painter. 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange PERMIT TRIVIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau, 'Le Douanier', painted in a naive, untrained style that is classed as this kind of painting.

clue.text: Like an island statue

parts.note: the Colossus, a wonder of the ancient world, stood on an Aegean island; the adjective for that island is needed

explanation.surface: Motionless as a sculpture on an isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a statue' suggests still or frozen, but the statue is the Colossus that stood at the harbour of Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to Rhodes, the Greek island famous for its Colossus.

clue.text: Notice porcelain it may not be genuine

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A warning that the antique vase you have spotted could be a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to think of forged china, but the definition is the last part: an appearance which may not be real.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming is outward appearance, a show that might be false rather than real.

clue.text: Matriarch and patriarch who produced 7

parts.note: a grandma is the matriarch of a family
Moses is one of the biblical patriarchs who led Israel

explanation.surface: An elderly couple who head their families produced something together.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is PRIMITIVE ART: Anna Mary Robertson Moses, known as Grandma Moses, was a self-taught American folk painter who began painting in her seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandma Moses was an American folk painter of the naive school, so she produced that style of painting.

clue.text: War dramatist gets medal at German stronghold

parts.note: MC, the Military Cross, is a British gallantry medal
a rath is an ancient Irish earthwork fort, a stronghold

explanation.surface: A playwright about war is decorated at an enemy fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: John McGrath wrote 'Events While Guarding the Bofors Gun', a play set among soldiers. 'at' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: John McGrath, Scottish playwright, wrote a celebrated drama about national servicemen guarding an anti-aircraft gun.

clue.text: Ms Sontag not applicable as apocryphal wife

parts.note: Susan Sontag was the American essayist
NA is the abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: An American critic is irrelevant to a story from the Apocrypha.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Apocrypha, Susanna, wife of Joakim, is falsely accused by two elders and saved by Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: Susanna is the virtuous married woman of the Book of Susanna, part of the biblical Apocrypha.

clue.text: Shelagh Delaney's was of Pooh Bear's choice

definitions.text: Shelagh Delaney's was of Pooh Bear's choice

parts.words: Shelagh Delaney's was of Pooh Bear's choice
parts.note: Shelagh Delaney's 1958 play is titled 'A ... of Honey', and honey is Winnie-the-Pooh's favourite food

explanation.surface: The playwright had the same preference as a famous storybook bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Delaney's play is 'A Taste of Honey'; Pooh Bear's choice is honey, so her play's title noun was 'of' honey.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sample of flavour, here the first noun in the title 'A Taste of Honey'.

clue.text: Shod like Felix Randal's horses?

parts.note: Hopkins's farrier Felix Randal fettled 'for the great grey drayhorse his bright and battering sandal', so the horse wore that open shoe

explanation.surface: How the blacksmith in a poem fitted out his horses' feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gerard Manley Hopkins's sonnet 'Felix Randal' the farrier made 'his bright and battering sandal' for the drayhorse, a horseshoe in poetic dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing open strapped shoes; Hopkins calls the drayhorse's horseshoe a sandal.

clue.text: He ended his days in deep reflection

definitions.text: He ended his days in deep reflection

parts.words: He ended his days in deep reflection
parts.note: the youth of Greek myth fell in love with his own image in a pool and pined away gazing into it

explanation.surface: A man who spent his final years lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep reflection' suggests contemplation, but it is a literal mirror image in the water, where the mythical youth wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ovid the beautiful youth died gazing at his own image in a pool and became a flower.

clue.text: It gets steamed up over Paris' manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres, as troops are moved about, says the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Something heats up above the French capital as an army drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges OVER and PARIS. 'It gets steamed up' looks like a description of anger, but the device turns liquid into vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: The device turns liquid into a fine vapour, often by heating, so steam is what it produces.

clue.text: Posthumous servant, "a sly and constant knave"

definitions.meaning: the faithful servant of Posthumus Leonatus in Shakespeare's Cymbeline, with Posthumus spelt as the adjective
the Queen in Cymbeline calls Posthumus's servant 'a sly and constant knave'

explanation.surface: A servant after death, described as cunning and loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posthumous' looks like 'after death', but it is Posthumus, hero of Shakespeare's 'Cymbeline', whose servant Pisanio the Queen calls 'a sly and constant knave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisanio is Posthumus Leonatus's loyal attendant in Cymbeline, described by the Queen in those words.

clue.text: Précis for the poorly

definitions.meaning: a summary or outline of the main points
unwell, tired and in poor health

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just links the two senses: a quick summary, and feeling worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a summary of key points; as an adjective it means exhausted and in poor health.

clue.text: A doctor in Georgia comes to a stop

indicators.note: in tells you to set the A and the doctor inside Georgia's abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A physician in the American South comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes to a stop' reads as halts; 'comes to' is a link and 'a stop' is the definition, an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamba is an organ register whose string tone imitates the viola da gamba.

clue.text: Somehow go zonal to find Neapolitan counsellor

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters of the next words are put together in some new way, an anagram

explanation.surface: Spreading out by zones somehow leads you to an Italian adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges GO ZONAL; Gonzalo is the honest old counsellor of Naples in Shakespeare's 'The Tempest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonzalo is the kindly old adviser to King Alonso of Naples in The Tempest.

clue.text: Lemur is set free in disorder happily orchestrated by court appointee

definitions.text: disorder happily orchestrated by court appointee

indicators.note: set free means the letters of the words before it are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A zoo animal escapes into chaos, with a royal official cheerfully in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' rearranges LEMUR IS. The Lord of Misrule was appointed at court to preside over Christmas revels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord of Misrule, an appointee of Tudor courts, presided over licensed Christmas revelry and disorder.

clue.text: Some sentences which parse nicely can be pretty lethal

indicators.note: some says only part of the words that follow is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A grammarian warns that well-formed sentences can kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The poison is concealed in 'parse nicely'; 'Some' points to that run. The surface suggests elegant prose, but it is a deadly element.
explanation.definitionFit: The element is a notorious poison, and its compounds have killed many.

clue.text: T. W. Robertson's class revealed in play

definitions.text: T. W. Robertson's class revealed in play

parts.words: T. W. Robertson's class revealed in play
parts.note: the Victorian dramatist T. W. Robertson wrote a play (1867) about a marriage across social ranks, named for a rigid social division

explanation.surface: A Victorian playwright's social rank shown on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: T. W. Robertson's comedy 'Caste' (1867) is about an aristocrat marrying a ballet dancer, so the class is revealed in the play's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social class, and the title of T. W. Robertson's 1867 comedy.

clue.text: His dramatic output was absurd

parts.note: a Romanian-French playwright was a leading figure of the Theatre of the Absurd

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a playwright's work as ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' sounds like a put-down but refers to the Theatre of the Absurd, of which Eugène Ionesco ('Rhinoceros', 'The Bald Soprano') was a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco wrote 'Rhinoceros' and 'The Bald Soprano', classics of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: "King Fog masses his molecules of carbon in squadrons in the city, while he scatters them — ly in the suburbs" (Israel Zangwill)

definitions.text: "King Fog masses his molecules of carbon in squadrons in the city, while he scatters them — ly in the suburbs" (Israel Zangwill)

parts.words: "King Fog masses his molecules of carbon in squadrons in the city, while he scatters them — ly in the suburbs" (Israel Zangwill)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation: the missing stem plus -ly means thinly or sparsely, the opposite of massed in squadrons

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist describes London fog as thick in town and thin in the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The gap takes an adjective which, with the printed '-ly', means thinly: Zangwill contrasts fog massed in the city with fog spread thin outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means thin or slight, so with -ly it describes fog scattered sparsely.

clue.text: A mold Bennett's monument gains time in law

indicators.note: gains means the monument takes in an extra letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Arnold Bennett (printed 'A mold' by a scanning slip) co-wrote the play 'The Statue', and a statue is a monument

explanation.surface: A novelist's memorial grows older under the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'A mold' for 'Arnold'. 'gains' puts T inside STATUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is an act passed by a legislature, a written law.

clue.text: Her husband was First Lord, though she was subject to 1 Across

definitions.text: Her husband was First Lord, though she was subject to 1 Across

parts.words: Her husband was First Lord, though she was subject to 1 Across
parts.note: Admiral Earl Howe was First Lord of the Admiralty, and his wife Mary sat for a famous full-length portrait by the painter of 1 across

explanation.surface: A wife who outranked no one at home, despite her husband's high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to' suggests obedience, but means she was the subject of a painting: Gainsborough's portrait 'Mary, Countess Howe' hangs at Kenwood House in London. Her husband, Richard Howe, was First Lord of the Admiralty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary, wife of Admiral Earl Howe, is the sitter in Gainsborough's famous portrait at Kenwood.
